query: For high-entropy nanoalloys in high-temperature applications, what governs structural and chemical stability, and why? Formulate one testable mechanistic hypothesis, propose a controlled comparison that would distinguish it from alternatives, predict observations relative to a baseline, define the boundaries of the prediction, identify supporting evidence from the background, and state a falsifying outcome.

generation.hypothesis: Thermally-activated diffusion and segregation of elements to grain boundaries lead to enhanced structural and chemical stability in high-entropy nanoalloys.
generation.intervention: Variation of annealing temperature (500-1000°C) and time (1-10 hours)
generation.structural_mediator: Grain boundary segregation and lattice distortion
generation.mechanism: Thermally-activated diffusion and segregation of elements to grain boundaries
generation.predicted_outcome: Improved high-temperature stability and resistance to oxidation and corrosion, compared to the baseline of unannealed or low-temperature annealed samples
generation.baseline: Unannealed or low-temperature annealed high-entropy nanoalloy samples
generation.boundary: The prediction is bounded by the specific range of annealing temperatures and times investigated, as well as the material system and operating conditions
